title: The Confession: panty liner vs underwear, 3D talking duet

format_analysis.format: AI 3D talking-object duet (Pixar-style; AD_RESEARCH F7 'AI skit / talking object'). A fussy, sheepish panty-liner character confesses to camera, and a calm, dry pair of plain black underwear answers. The 3D characters sit in photoreal sets that change on every line, and the cut includes real product inserts.
format_analysis.how_it_should_look: Pixar-quality 3D characters (soft subsurface, big glossy eyes, appealing not grotesque) composited into photoreal, warm golden-hour sets. Warm Cream walls and shelf; Claret used once per frame (the hand towel, later the button); a plum handbag lining. Shallow depth of field. The base is a 35mm eye-level animated-film camera (smooth, locked or gently moving, not handheld), broken up by dramatic angle changes: a wide-lens ECU lunge, a low-angle hero, a top-down deflated shot and over-the-shoulders, plus 110-125% edit punch-ins on emphasis words. Real product inserts are owned-phone in natural window light, graded warm to match the sets. Captions are built in CapCut only. The hook is a Claret pill with cream Hanken Grotesk ExtraBold at ~20% height. Dialogue sits in a per-phrase Warm Cream box with Plum Ink text at ~55% (1-4 words, word-locked), with small 'panty liner' and 'underwear' tags on first appearance. Fraunces appears only on the end-card brand line, and all text stays inside the 14-62% height safe zone. Sound: an off-screen ACHOO sting, light comedic foley on every action (paper rustle, peel, skid, boing, lid tap, zip, with no crinkle on the liner), a soft warm licensed acoustic bed, and two clearly different character voices.
format_analysis.runtime_main: 30.0s. The script says ~22s, but its locked dialogue (85 words after the word swaps) can't fit 22s at any natural pace; see pacing_check.vo_fit_issues. Five edit-only trims bring it to ~26s.
format_analysis.build_profile: 0-3.9s HOOK: the 3D liner on camera (Veo native voice -> ElevenLabs Voice Changer, LINER voice) + an off-screen library ACHOO. No human on screen, so no Dramatization label. 3.9-9.9s: the liner on camera across 3 rooms (shelf, handbag, bin), with one silent underwear reaction cutaway at 4.7s. 9.9-15.4s: the underwear on camera (UNDERWEAR voice) + 1 real product insert + the liner's side-eye. 15.4-21.5s: faceless. The underwear's VO is ElevenLabs TTS in the same saved voice, with no lip-sync, over 3 owned-phone/AI product inserts, the AI 'left behind' gag and the AI woman shot waist-to-knee. 21.5-25.65s: duet. The liner on camera, then 'And you?' with its back to camera (no lip-sync), then the underwear answers + 1 real insert. 25.65-30.0s: END CARD, with the underwear speaking the CTA; text and button in CapCut. The only human voice is the off-screen ACHOO SFX.

reference_ads.what_we_take: UltraDries Pixar (#4 by impressions, 104d): the talking pad hops to a NEW ROOM and changes size/angle on every cut (living room -> vanity -> bedroom -> kitchen table), with word-locked captions. We hop rooms whenever a line names a place (handbag at 1.65s, bin at 7.95s and 21.5s) and change angle on every other line. NOT its yellowed/stained pad, its 'you' copy or its 5.8s opening hold.

Everdries talking pad, liner and diaper (208d): each object owns a room, and there's one pill caption per phrase. Frame 0 shows a visible 'Veo' watermark, so the Veo-native voice path is proven on object faces. NOT its ~7s single-angle hold per speaker: our longest talking hold is 2.25s, and every line gets a new angle.

UltraDries pad vs underwear duet (180d): the two-shot blocking, the underwear with its face on its front panel (ours sits higher, just under the waistband), the reframe onto whoever is speaking, and the cut from the talking two-shot to the REAL product (our S12 at 11.4s). NOT its stained pad, 'leak proof / 100 mL' claims, pour demo or 3.9s+ static two-shots.
UltraDries #6 (VO over b-roll): pacing only. Every cut brings a new subject or location, with 8 cuts in 3-10s. Our 3-10s also has 8 cuts, and no room repeats on back-to-back lines.

recommended.text: Sneeze-pee 🤧  ->  Her panty liner has a confession
recommended.on_screen_timing: 0.00-0.80s 'Sneeze-pee 🤧' (the emoji pops at 0.10s on the jolt); 0.80-3.90s 'Her panty liner has a confession' (it swaps as the liner hits the lens and stays through the handbag hop).
recommended.style: Claret #A33154 pill with Warm Cream Hanken Grotesk ExtraBold text, ~64px at 1080w, centred at ~20% height inside the 4:5 safe zone. No dialogue caption under it until 3.9s.
recommended.why: Chunk 1 names the moment and the word pee in one word, readable in ~0.3s, so a stranger can't read it as period or panty-line content. Dropping the locked '?' keeps it a moment label rather than a question about the viewer's condition (Meta personal-attributes rule). Chunk 2 does three jobs: it gives the first on-screen 'panty liner' (word rule), uses the third person ('her'), and opens a curiosity gap that the liner pays off at 3.9-6.65s ('I'm not even underwear. I'm a sticker.'). It's built on the most-proven animated opener in the niche, UltraDries 1400650075258672 'I'm your disposable pad... I need to be honest with you' (#4 by impressions, 104d): the object's confession, minus the worn phrase and minus 'you'. It also beats the locked text because the locked chunks (0.4s and 0.7s) sit under the ~0.5s read time, and 'the liner she keeps in her bag' only describes what the dialogue already says, so it opens no gap.

alternates.text: Sneeze-pee 🤧  ->  I'm a panty liner. I bunch. I shift.
alternates.why: The object introduces itself and names its flaws in frame 1. It leads with the CJ-safe form-only enemy (bunch, shift; no 'fails'). It's first person from an OBJECT, so it says nothing about the viewer. It's a weaker gap than 'confession' because it spends the self-roast up front, but it's the closest copy of a 208-day talking-object winner.
alternates.proven_anchor: Everdries AI talking pad 1700150534480418: 'I'm a bulky pad. I contain your bladder leaks, but I bunch up, shift out of place...' (208d). 'your bladder leaks' is dropped for the Meta rule.

alternates.text: It's 2026.  ->  Why is her sneeze-pee plan a panty liner? 🤧
alternates.why: The contrarian date hook makes the old habit feel out of date with no shame and no viewer question ('her', not 'you'). 🤧 replaces 🤢 (no gross-out). Caveats: V1-a already uses this anchor ('It's 2026... Why is a liner still the plan for sneeze-pee?'), so running it here muddies the V1 vs V2 test. It also has to be bumped to 2027 in January.
alternates.proven_anchor: Everdries 1206351388295667: 'It's 2025! Why are you still using pads? 🤢 / Pads weren't designed to be an incontinence solution' (275d, 6 dupes, #14 by impressions). Only the first line is copied, and the 'you' is swapped for 'her'.

alternates.text: Sneezing shouldn't require crossing your legs.
alternates.why: It's a 30-45 proven moment line that passes the Meta rule as written (AD_RESEARCH §3) and names the sneeze. It sets up the underwear's identity line ('for women who'd rather laugh than cross their legs'), so the ad closes its own loop. It's weaker on cartoon-specific curiosity, and it doesn't say 'pee'.
alternates.proven_anchor: Pelvic-clinic hook 'Sneezing shouldn't require crossing your legs.' (112d, AD_RESEARCH §3 'Hooks proven on 30-45 women'), used verbatim.

text_hook.note: The RECOMMENDED text differs from the locked script ('sneeze-pee?' 0-0.4s / 'the liner she keeps in her bag' 0.5-1.2s). It keeps the coined 'sneeze-pee', removes the '?', adds 'panty liner' and the confession gap, and holds the chunks long enough to read. Nikita chiefs it. If he keeps the locked text, the word rule makes chunk 2 'the panty liner she keeps in her bag', held 0.80-3.90s.

visual_hook_build.miro: #117 3D Talking Character, opened as #70 Face Lean-In to Lens (+ an audio-only ACHOO sting)
visual_hook_build.frame_1: 9:16, bright golden hour, NOT static. A Warm Cream bathroom shelf (Claret hand towel at left, frosted toothbrush cup, hair tie, mini white pedal bin soft at the far right). Centre-left at ~45% height, the clean white, unbranded, wingless oval panty-liner character is caught 2-3 frames into its startled jolt: feet off the shelf, stubby arms flung up, big brown eyes wide, motion blur on the arms. The plain black underwear character dozes in deep soft focus at frame-right with its eyes closed. The Claret pill 'Sneeze-pee 🤧' sits at ~20% height, the ACHOO is on the audio track, and a small 'AI-generated' tag sits lower-left. No mirror, no human, no text inside the AI image.
build_steps: 1. LOCK THE PRODUCT FIRST (blocked): shoot the 5 CJ sample photos (flat front, flat back, side, stretched, under leggings). Build the UNDERWEAR character sheet in Nano Banana Pro from those photos only. The garment stays unchanged: rise, waistband width, leg line and matte sheen are copied from the photos, not described in text. Add one Pixar face on the UPPER FRONT panel just under the waistband (two soft eyes, small mouth), with nothing on the lower front or gusset. No arms: it moves by hopping and leaning like the UltraDries duet, and fewer limbs means less drift. Views: front, 3/4, side, back (no face). Expressions: dozing (eyes closed), one eye open, dry eyebrow raise, calm half-smile, talking, wink. Register it as a reusable reference element 'UNDIES'. Nikita checks it against the real sample before anything else uses it.

2. BUILD THE LINER CHARACTER SHEET (can start now): one thin, clean white, unbranded, wingless oval panty liner with soft matte quilting; no print, no channels, no colour. It wears a backing-paper strip on its back like a little cape (for the 'sticker' gag). Big soft brown Pixar eyes and expressive brows in its top third, a small mouth, two short stubby arms and tiny feet in the same white material (no gloves). Expressions: startled, fussy-talking, sheepish, scrunched, side-eye, deflated, sulking. Register it as element 'LINER'. Keep it appealing, not grotesque: the Everdries/UltraDries villain faces are not our tone, because the joke is on the liner, not on her.

3. BUILD 5 EMPTY SET PLATES with one light setup (low golden-hour window light from frame-left, Warm Cream walls and shelf, Claret only in the towel): (a) HOME BASE bathroom shelf with a mini white countertop pedal bin at the end; (b) handbag interior (plum lining, keys, lip balm, phone edge, folded tissue, no logo); (c) bin side view, lid up; (d) bin top-down, clean empty white bag; (e) END plate, the shelf with the top 40% left as clean wall for text.

4. BUILD THE ANGLE LIBRARY as start frames (elements composited into plates, 9:16, 2K). LINER: LIN-1 hook MCU at rest on the shelf edge, 35mm eye-level, underwear dozing soft at right; LIN-2 handbag, low angle from inside the bag; LIN-3 shelf MCU 3/4; LIN-4 shelf MCU front; LIN-5 low tabletop angle along the shelf; LIN-6 bin rim side MCU; LIN-7 top-down inside the bin (high angle); LIN-8 high-angle deflated on the closed bin lid; LIN-9 over the underwear's waistband edge onto the liner. UNDERWEAR: UND-1 CU reaction; UND-2 wide two-shot (liner peeking from the bin); UND-3 low-angle hero; UND-4 eye-level CU; UND-5 over the liner's backing-paper back. Plus the END two-shot and the F17 'left behind' frame. Free extra angles: 110-125% punch-ins on F5, F14, F20, F23 and F25. Rule: no talking angle is reused on back-to-back lines.

5. HOOK MOTION: start frame = LIN-1 at rest. Generate ONE Veo 3.1 image-to-video clip (4s) with the action and the line together: a startled jump straight up, a landing, a head-whip to camera, a rush at the lens until the eyes fill the frame (wide-lens bulge), then 'That's my cue.' Dialogue only: no music, and no sneeze inside the gen, because the ACHOO is added in the edit. In CapCut, put the ACHOO on frame 0, trim the head so frame 0 is 2-3 frames into the jolt, add a 3-frame shake when the lunge stops, and cut at 1.65s.

6. VOICE PATH, RECOMMENDED (Path A): each talking clip is a Veo 3.1 image-to-video clip with ONE speaker saying ONE line, while the other character only reacts. Then run each clip's audio through ElevenLabs Voice Changer into two saved voices. LINER: higher, fussy, quick (~4 words/s). UNDERWEAR: warm, dry, calm mid-30s (~3 words/s). Voice Changer keeps the timing, so Veo's native mouth sync still holds while both voices stay identical across all 14 clips. Off-screen lines (the underwear's 'Nothing to stick... cross their legs' VO and the liner's 'And you?' from behind) are ElevenLabs TTS in the same two saved voices, with no lip-sync. WHY Path A: (1) these are non-human faces, and face-detecting lip-sync tools often refuse or smear on a liner or a pair of underwear; (2) Veo makes the mouth, the motion and the audio timing in one pass, so there's no second lip-sync pass to fail; (3) the talking-object ref 1700150534480418 carries a Veo watermark, so the pipeline is proven on exactly this kind of ad. FALLBACK (Path B), for any line Veo garbles twice: generate the ElevenLabs line first, then Hedra Character-3 lip-sync (handles stylised faces) on that angle's start frame. Never lip-sync two faces from one track.

7. EDIT: one line = one angle or room, with word-locked cuts and an SFX on every cut to 10s. All captions, labels, the AI tags and the end card are built in CapCut. Keep C2PA on export. Nikita checks every underwear frame against the sample before export.
visual_hook_build.lane_and_tool: AI start frame + motion. Nano Banana Pro (Higgsfield, 9:16 2K) for the character sheets, plates and start frames; Veo 3.1 image-to-video with native dialogue for the 14 talking clips; Kling 2.x for 3 silent motion shots; ElevenLabs Voice Changer + TTS for the two saved voices; CapCut for text and punch-ins. Owned-phone for 4 real product inserts. All tool picks are recommendations until Nikita confirms the generator.
visual_hook_build.fallback: If Veo won't hold the liner's design or the lunge: use Kling 2.x start/end frames (rest MCU -> eyes-fill-frame ECU), add the ElevenLabs line with Hedra Character-3 lip-sync, and if the lunge still fails, do it in the edit (a 100->140% scale ramp over 0.45s + a 3-frame shake + a whoosh on the rest clip). If the CJ photos aren't in yet: build and approve the liner-only shots (F1-F3, F5-F9, F17, F21), all plates, and a full timed animatic with a grey underwear placeholder (never exported). Only the underwear passes then wait on the photos.
failure_modes_to_reject: Garbled, mushy or rubbery mouth; the mouth moving on the NON-speaking character; extra, changed or dropped words; Veo-added music, laughs or a sneeze inside the gen.

A liner with ANY yellow or cream tint, a stain, a wet look, blue or pink channels, wings, print, or anything resembling a real brand (Always/Carefree/Poise). The UltraDries refs' yellowed pads are exactly what we don't do.
Underwear with lace, a logo, a tag, seams or a gusset that isn't on the sample; drift in sheen, rise, waistband width or colour; a boyshort or thong morph; the inside of a leg opening shown.
The underwear's face placed on the crotch, gusset or lower front. It must sit on the upper front just under the waistband.
Either character's design changing between clips (eye colour, quilting, proportions). Re-generate from the element; never patch it with prompt text.
A grotesque or villain face (the Everdries look). The liner is sheepish and fussy, never gross.
The liner looking at the lens on 'And you?', or 'And you?' appearing as a caption.
Any human face, mirror or reflection in the hook. A static or dark frame 0.
AI woman: a crotch- or butt-centred crop, a face in frame, a mirror, seated, a sneeze/laugh/jump acted, or the top not covering the hip.
AI hand: extra or fused fingers, or a handbag that sprouts a logo or branded hardware.
Any text generated inside an AI frame (all text goes on in CapCut).

shots.angle_or_room: HOME BASE: warm bathroom shelf, golden hour. Eye-level 35mm at shelf height.
shots.what_we_see: Warm Cream shelf and wall in low golden window light from frame-left: a folded Claret hand towel at the left edge, a frosted toothbrush cup, a hair tie, and a mini white pedal bin soft at the far right end. Centre-left on the shelf edge at ~45% height: the PANTY-LINER character. It is clean white, unbranded, wingless and oval, with soft matte quilting, big brown Pixar eyes in its top third, a small mouth, two stubby arms and a backing-paper strip on its back worn like a little cape. Frame 0 is already 2-3 frames into the jolt: both feet off the shelf, arms flung up, eyes wide, motion blur on the arms. Behind it at frame-right, in deep soft focus: the plain black UNDERWEAR character, folded upright, eyes closed (dozing). Bright frame, no mirror, no human.
shots.motion_inside_shot: Event 1 (0.03s): it jolts straight up at the off-screen ACHOO. Event 2 (0.40-0.85s): it lands, whips its head to camera and rushes the lens until its eyes fill the frame. The wide lens bulges the face and the underwear blurs out (Miro #70). Event 3 (0.80s): the hook pill swaps text while it says 'That's my cue.' nose-to-lens with a tiny wobble. 3-frame shake on the lunge's stop.
shots.on_screen_text: 0.00-0.80 Claret pill, cream Hanken Grotesk ExtraBold, centred ~20% height: 'Sneeze-pee 🤧' (the emoji pops at 0.10s). 0.80-3.90, same pill: 'Her panty liner has a confession'. Locked-script alt if Nikita keeps it: 'sneeze-pee?' / 'the panty liner she keeps in her bag'. small 'AI-generated' tag lower-left at ~61% height (on every character frame).
shots.vo_or_dialogue: (off-screen woman, library SFX) 'ACHOO!' 0.00-0.35 / LINER (higher, fussy, fast) 0.85-1.55: "That's my cue."
shots.sfx: ACHOO sting on frame 0 (Meta Sound Collection or a licensed library). Tiny startled squeak at 0.05s. Whoosh on the lunge at 0.40s. Warm acoustic bed fades in from 0.3s. Quiet bathroom room tone.
shots.cut_reason: Cuts on the end of 'cue'. The next line names a place ('her bag'), so we jump there. At 1.65s the hook stays one continuous shot with 3 motion events (pacing law ~1.5-3s).
shots.tool_rec: Start frame LIN-1: Nano Banana Pro (Higgsfield, 9:16, 2K) = shelf plate + LINER element. Motion + line: Veo 3.1 image-to-video, 4s, native dialogue, one speaker. In CapCut, trim the head so frame 0 is mid-jolt and lay the ACHOO on frame 0. Fallback: Kling 2.x start/end frame (rest MCU -> eyes-fill-frame ECU) + Hedra lip-sync, or a 100->140% edit push-in over 0.45s on the rest clip.
shots.blocked_on: Only the soft-focus underwear in the background needs the CJ photos. Make the frame now with that slot empty and comp it in later (deep soft focus is forgiving).

The panty liner perches on the keys like a little stage, with warm window light spilling in through the opening above. It pats the lining like this is home.
shots.motion_inside_shot: 6-frame whip-zoom transition in. The liner sweeps a stubby arm around the bag on 'in her bag', and the keys jingle as it shifts. 108% in-shot bump on 'bag'. Slow 5% push-in throughout.
shots.on_screen_text: The hook pill continues: 'Her panty liner has a confession'. No separate caption: the pill carries this line sound-off. small 'AI-generated' tag lower-left at ~61% height (on every character frame).
shots.vo_or_dialogue: LINER: "I'm the panty liner she keeps in her bag."
shots.sfx: Whoosh on the cut. Muffled bag-interior room tone. Key jingle on 'bag'.
shots.cut_reason: The line is complete and the hook pill clears at 3.90s. The next line ('Thing is...') goes back to home base.

shots.angle_or_room: HOME BASE shelf, 3/4 from frame-right.

Its face sits on the upper front panel just under the waistband (two soft eyes, a small mouth), with nothing on the lower front. It opens one eye and slowly raises one eyebrow at what the liner just said.

pacing_check.broll_or_insert_share: 45% off the home-base shelf (real-look/product inserts 7.75s = 26% + location hops 5.85s = 20%); non-two-shot coverage 81% (only F10, F22 and the end card are two-shots)
vo_fit_issues: WHOLE AD, the biggest finding: the locked dialogue is 85 words after the word swaps (liner 40, underwear 45; 84 as written). At the brief's 2.4 words/s that's ~35s of speech. The script's ~22s main cut would need ~3.9 words/s from BOTH characters with no pauses, while the 'calm, dry' underwear says 45 of them. It can't be built as timed. This board keeps EVERY locked line and times it at the refs' measured talking-character pace: the liner at ~4 w/s (the UltraDries #4 pad opens at 4.1-4.3 w/s; the Everdries pad runs at 3.7) and the underwear at ~3 w/s (the UltraDries duet underwear runs at 2.9-3.4). That gives 30.0s.

Per-beat slip vs the script's clock: beat 1 (script 0-1.2s, 12 words) -> board 0.85-3.80s; beat 2 (1.2-3.0s, 9) -> 3.90-6.55s; beat 3 (3.0-6.0s, 11) -> 6.65-9.75s; beat 4 (6.0-9.5s, 13) -> 10.10-15.35s; beat 5 (9.5-15.0s, 17) -> 15.40-21.40s; beat 6 (15.0-17.5s, 11) -> 21.50-25.55s; beat 7 (17.5-22.0s, 12) -> 25.75-29.45s. The underwear's spoken reveal ('Hi.') moves from ~6s to 10.1s. To keep the script's 'product on screen by ~6s' goal, the board cuts to the underwear's sharp reaction CU at 4.70s (F4), and it's in soft focus from frame 0.

Tightest shots: F1 'That's my cue.' (3 words in 0.7s of speech, fussy-fast by design); F2 9 words / 2.25s = 4.0 w/s (liner); F8 3 words / 0.8s. Underwear shots all sit at 2.5-3.2 w/s. If an ElevenLabs/Voice Changer take for the liner runs slower than ~4 w/s, each liner line adds ~0.2-0.4s. Set the liner's speed first, then re-time.

PROPOSED TRIMS (Nikita chiefs; NOT applied in this board). All are edit-only, because each sentence is its own clip/shot and nothing has to be regenerated: T1 drop 'Thing is...' (cut F3, -0.8s; the confession still reads); T2 drop 'I'm underwear.' so the line becomes 'Hi. Plain black underwear. Not a pad. Not a diaper.' (cut F11, -0.75s; this also removes the doubled 'underwear' the word swap created); T3 drop the SPOKEN 'Not a pad, not a diaper.' from the CTA, since it stays on the card twice and was already said at 12.5-14.75s (the end card drops to ~2.5s, so hold it to 3.0s: net -1.35s); T4 drop 'So...' (-0.5s); T5 drop 'Just underwear.' (cut S18, -0.8s; the headline still says it). Result: ~25.8s. A true 22s would also need the 'So... I'm in the trash / And you? / Wash. Hang. Wear again.' exchange cut (-4.15s), which loses the reuse payoff. Not recommended.
pacing_check.notes: How this beats the refs: the hook is one continuous 1.65s shot with 3 motion events (jolt, lunge, text swap), where the UltraDries #4 Pixar holds 5.8s with almost no motion. The 3-10s section has 8 cuts (= the #6 winner), against 1-2 in the talking-object refs. EVERY line gets a new angle or a new room (the #4's room-hops, but per line instead of per ~3s), so no talking angle holds more than 2.25s and no angle repeats on back-to-back lines. Everdries' ~7s single-angle holds are the anti-pattern we avoid. 45% of runtime is off the home-base shelf, and the real product is on screen at 11.4s (sharp character version at 4.7s). The 10s+ section cuts faster than the law's 2-3s because Nikita asked for an angle change on every line, and 5 of those changes are free edit punch-ins. LONG CUT (~40s): adds the second off-screen-ACHOO beat in the bin ('Sneeze-pee? That's my cue-' / '...and back in the trash.'), a second under-leggings walk-out insert, and the underwear's 'Still just underwear.' before the end card. See compliance_flags: that ACHOO has to move before the reveal.
